column3: The Hebrew repeats “that soul” as the subject of being cut off.
The Hebrew says they found a man, rather than expressing the finding passively.
The Hebrew separately states “and he died” after the stoning.
The Hebrew begins “and,” without an explicit “later.”
The tassel and the object looked at are singular in the Hebrew.
The Hebrew introduces a purpose with “so that,” rather than simply a result with “then.”
